title: fix(hono-server): apply the baseline additively on `/auth/me/permissions` and `/me/apps` (#7608)
body:
Fixes #7608

## The defect

Both permission resolutions in `packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/current-user-endpoints.ts` applied the deployment baseline only in a **second** `resolvePermissionSets` call gated on emptiness:

```ts
:767   if (resolved.length === 0 && fallbackNames.length > 0) {    // /auth/me/permissions
:978   if (resolved.length === 0 && fallbackNames.length > 0) {    // /me/apps
```

That is the fallback **cliff** ADR-0090 D5 abolishes, verbatim:

> The fallback cliff is abolished. Today's semantics ("fallback applies only while the user has *zero* explicit grants") mean the first real grant silently removes the user's baseline. `everyone` is additive like any other position: baseline ∪ explicit, always.

`SecurityPlugin.resolvePermissionSetsForContext` — the **data** plane, one function call away — has pushed the baseline into `requested` and resolved once for as long as D5 has existed. These two endpoints had not, so the planes disagreed the moment a member held any explicit grant.

PR #7605 (#7555) landed as `9c82146d1` and changed *which* names these sites resolve while leaving the guard untouched, exactly as the card predicted. Both cliffs were confirmed verbatim on `main` before this change.

## The user-visible effect, measured

Both numbers come from the fixture shipped with this PR — a member of one org, a baseline granting two capabilities across two apps, and one explicit grant adding a third. The "before" column was measured by reverting the source change and re-running these same cases.

| `/me/apps` | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| member with **zero** grants | `home`, `reports` (2) | `home`, `reports` (2) — unchanged |
| member with **one** explicit grant | `exports` (1) | `exports`, `home`, `reports` (**3**) |
| effect of receiving the first grant | **−1 app** (2 → 1) | **+1 app** (2 → 3) |

**+2 apps appear that did not before**, and the two baseline apps are retained rather than traded away for the granted one.

On `/auth/me/permissions`, the same member regains **1 readable object**, **1 readable field** and **2 capabilities**, and `permissionSets` goes from `['showcase_ops']` to `['member_default', 'showcase_ops']`. The endpoint had been reporting object/field access *narrower* than a read actually returns.

Fail-direction was **closed** — the console hid what the API allowed — which is why this read as cosmetic for as long as it did.

## The change

The baseline names go into `requested` before the **single** resolution, via one shared `effectivePermissionSetNames` helper both handlers call. That retires the second `resolvePermissionSets` call outright rather than merely widening its guard: once the baseline is an input to the first call, a second call over a *subset* of those same names can add nothing.

No `principalKind === 'agent'` branch, unlike the plugin's copy — a property of this surface, not an omission. D10 withholds the human baseline from an agent because its ceiling must stay exactly its scope-derived set; these endpoints are reached only through `makeExecutionContextResolver`, which resolves a better-auth **session** and never marks a principal kind. An agent has no session to present here, so the branch would be unreachable code.

## The structural question the card asked

> should these endpoints stop re-implementing this resolution at all and call the plugin's own service?

**Measured, and deliberately not done in this PR** — with the reason, rather than silently keeping the copy.

The published `ISecurityService` exposes `resolvePermissionSetNames(context)`, which returns **names only**. Both handlers need the full resolved sets (`objects`, `fields`, `systemPermissions`, `tabPermissions`) to run their merges, so today's contract cannot serve them. De-duplicating means adding `resolvePermissionSetsForContext` to the contract — `packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts` plus its exhaustive-method contract test, `plugin-security`'s registered service literal (the method is `private` today), and a call site here: **3 packages, ~5 files**, against this card's 1 file + 1 test.

Two things make it a net *addition* rather than a removal, which is what tips it:

1. **The contract requires feature-detection.** `ISecurityService` is consumed as `Partial<ISecurityService>` precisely so a consumer degrades rather than assuming the full surface. So this file would have to keep the local resolution as the fallback for a SecurityPlugin too old to carry the method — leaving the copy **plus** the delegation **plus** a branch between them, until that fallback can be dropped.
2. **The two are not actually the same resolution.** The plugin resolves through `this.metadata` / `this.bootstrapPermissionSets` / `this.dbLoader`; these endpoints pass their own loaders, and `/me/apps` deliberately projects a *narrower* column set than `/auth/me/permissions` does. Delegating changes which columns get loaded on both surfaces — a behaviour change well beyond a cliff fix, and one that wants its own measurement.

What this PR does instead is shrink the drift surface where it is cheap: the rule is now **one named function** in this file, documented against `SecurityPlugin.resolvePermissionSetsForContext` by name and quoting D5, rather than two inline guards that drifted independently. The remaining duplication is real and worth a follow-up card; it is not worth a 3-package contract change riding on a bug fix.

One stale cross-reference is left untouched deliberately: `plugin-security`'s `resolveFallbackPermissionSets` doc-comment describes "the second step `/auth/me/permissions` takes … (`resolved.length === 0 && fallbackName`)", which this PR deletes. Correcting it is a comment-only edit in a package outside this card's file surface and currently hot from #7555 — flagged rather than folded in.

## Tests

New: `packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/current-user-endpoints-additive-baseline.test.ts` — 12 cases, all driving the real HTTP surface and counting what a member **sees**, never just asserting the guard changed.

The fixtures bind the baseline set to **no** position and supply it via `security.baselinePermissionSets`, deliberately: `resolveUserAuthzGrants` already expands the implicit `everyone` position, so a fixture delivering the baseline that way would have passed before and after. The service channel is the one the cliff gated.

**Mutation table** — every case proven to fail, each by a named mutation:

| mutation | cases killed |
|---|---|
| **revert** — restore both `resolved.length === 0` guards (pre-fix source) | 8 of 12 |
| **M-A** — drop the additive push from `effectivePermissionSetNames` | 8 (incl. both zero-grant pins) |
| **M-B** — drop the `!requested.includes(name)` dedup | 1 (baseline-held-explicitly) |
| **M-C** — treat an empty declared baseline as unset | 1 (empty-baseline deployment) |
| **M-D** — `/me/apps` stops enforcing `requiredPermissions` | 7 (incl. the fail-open control) |

All 12 are killed by at least one mutation; the source was verified byte-identical to the fixed version after the last revert, so no mutation residue reached the commit.

The two "unchanged by this fix" pins matter: without them, deleting the baseline everywhere would pass every case that only asserts the one-grant member *gained* things. M-A is exactly that mutation, and it kills both.

## Verification

- `pnpm lint` — clean
- `pnpm typecheck` — 126/126 tasks pass
- `plugin-hono-server` — 199 tests pass (17 files)
- `plugin-security` — 952 tests pass (46 files), the sibling plane unaffected
- `packages/qa/dogfood/test/me-apps-and-everyone-baseline.dogfood.test.ts` — 6 pass on the **served showcase stack** (real boot, real sign-in, real `/me/apps`), the closest existing coverage of this endpoint

Changeset included. No `content/docs/releases/**` edits. `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts` untouched.
